NSAID (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) is a class of pharmaceutical medications. In the context of the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database's 2022–2023 annual report, NSAIDs are identified as a notable risk factor for severe bleeding complications in patients treated for atrial fibrillation [^src1]. 

The report highlights that avoiding the use of NSAIDs is a key behavioral and clinical intervention to reduce the incidence of severe bleeding events. Specifically, it notes that increased attention to avoiding NSAIDs and platelet inhibitors, combined with better blood pressure control and a reduction in the population's alcohol consumption, is expected to lead to fewer intracranial hemorrhages [^src1]. 

Because the provided corpus is limited, NSAID is mentioned only once in this context. No further details, relationships, or timeline events involving this pharmaceutical class are available.

## Mentions

- Page 66: "Desuden vil den øgede opmærksomhed på ikke at anvende pladehæmmere og NSAID samt bedre kontrol af blodtryk og reduktion af befolkningens alkoholforbrug lede til færre intrakranielle blødninger." [^src1]
